title: HB580 (2023 Regular): Election Law – Polling Sites – Firearms Prohibitions

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Maryland text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2023RS/bills/hb/hb0580f.pdf)
provenance.note: First reader (as filed); no passage vote recorded.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Election Law § 16–904(b)): EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SUBSECTION (C) OF THIS SECTION AND § 16–903 OF THIS SUBTITLE, A PERSON MAY NOT: (1) CARRY OR DISPLAY A FIREARM ON THE PREMISES OF A PRIVATELY OR PUBLICLY OWNED BUILDING BEING USED AS A POLLING SITE DURING AN ELECTION, INCLUDING IN A PARKING LOT; OR (2) CARRY OR POSSESS A FIREARM WITHIN 100 FEET OF A POLLING SITE DURING AN ELECTION.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Election Law § 16–904(c)(1)): AN INDIVIDUAL IS NOT IN VIOLATION OF SUBSECTION (B) OF THIS SECTION IF THE INDIVIDUAL IS: (I) A LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER IN THE REGULAR COURSE OF THE OFFICER’S DUTY; OR (II) AN OFF–DUTY LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER, IF: 1. THE OFFICER IS DISPLAYING THE OFFICER’S BADGE OR CREDENTIAL; AND 2. THE WEAPON CARRIED OR POSSESSED BY THE OFFICER IS CONCEALED.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Election Law § 16–904(d)(1)): A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SECTION IS SUBJECT TO A CIVIL PENALTY NOT EXCEEDING $5,000.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Election Law § 16–903(a)(3)): except as required by law or by regulation adopted by the State Board in connection with ballot security activities, carrying or displaying a FIREARM, AS DEFINED IN § 16–904(A) OF THIS SUBTITLE, or badge within 100 feet of a polling site on election day.
